heading: Unexplained SAE reconstruction error mostly reflects training artifacts
definition: dark matter mostly reflects how SAEs are trained (sparsity penalty, shrinkage, dead latents, objective) and shrinks with better architectures or end-to-end training, rather than reflecting structure in the model's representation.
summary: Training and architecture changes can reduce SAE error, but whether they explain most of the reconstruction error called “dark matter” remains contested. Better downstream behavior does not consistently imply lower activation error, and substantial error that affects model behavior can persist.

suggested_status.by_scale: <1B: C for the activation-error reduction component, with partial training-dependent improvements demonstrated; majority attribution remains unresolved. 1-10B: C, with training-dependent improvements alongside increased activation error or persistent functional error; majority attribution remains unresolved. Toy, 10-100B and >100B: ?; no corresponding size-identified coverage in versions.V6.studies_by_size.
suggested_status.reason: The broad statement remains contested; narrower training dependence is supported, while predominant causal attribution is unresolved. Input counts, before checker relabeling: versions.V6.verdicts.supports.studies=8, versions.V6.verdicts.limits_scope.studies=11 and versions.V6.verdicts.challenges.studies=6; these categories overlap. GPT-2 small layer-8 refinement improves reconstruction and downstream cross-entropy but closes only part of the ReLU–TopK gap, warranting limits_scope rather than support for majority attribution (arXiv:2406.04093#r5, arXiv:2406.04093#r6). On GPT2-small, end-to-end variants reconstruct activation directions worse than local SAEs at similar CE loss increase (arXiv:2405.12241#r19, arXiv:2405.12241#r20). Lower output CE measures a different construct, and evaluation-time normalization does not establish reduced activation error relative to local training. On Gemma-2-2B, encoder tuning and the best full-replacement method substantially reduce downstream divergence, supporting the narrower error-shrinkage component; remaining divergence alone is not a limitation of that component (lw:4tEnmAwFNtz9zJ6cz#r11, lw:4tEnmAwFNtz9zJ6cz#r21, lw:4tEnmAwFNtz9zJ6cz#r22). Separately, pre-encoder-tuned modifications increase single-layer RRE (lw:4tEnmAwFNtz9zJ6cz#r20). On Gemma 2 2B base/chat crosscoders, removing a specific shrinkage artifact leaves substantial behaviourally relevant error (arXiv:2504.02922#R1, arXiv:2504.02922#R2, arXiv:2504.02922#R3, arXiv:2504.02922#R4, arXiv:2504.02922#R9, arXiv:2504.02922#R10).
suggested_status.open_questions: A matched intervention that removes most activation error and its downstream consequences, separately measures linear and nonlinear residual components, and quantifies training causes versus representation structure would change the assessment. Generalization beyond restricted activation datasets and the size bins in versions.V6.studies_by_size remains open.

source.title: Decomposing The Dark Matter of Sparse Autoencoders
source.authors: Joshua Engels; L. Smith; Max Tegmark

original_result.setup: On Gemma 2 9B layer 20, the study applied gradient pursuit at inference time to iteratively adjust feature activations using gradients with a frozen Gemma Scope SAE decoder, keeping the number of active features (L0) fixed.
original_result.result: Total fraction of variance unexplained decreased by 3–5%, while its nonlinear component stayed almost constant.
original_result.interpretation: This is the displayed original-result block, not a guarantee that the original tested every part of this claim.

sources.headline: BatchTopK nearly eliminated chat-only information leakage into base reconstruction error.
Removing the sparsity penalty corrected overly small feature activations and partially recovered downstream performance.
JumpReLU TSAEs nearly eliminated reconstruction error on static entity activations.
Training and encoder improvements reduced full-replacement KL divergence by over an order of magnitude.
TopK improved reconstruction scaling, while refinement partially corrected L1's tendency to underestimate feature activations.
Gated SAEs improved reconstruction over L1 baselines at equal compute.
Cosine scoring corrected severe reconstruction failures on high-norm Qwen3-8B activations.
Gradient-pursuit inference improved loss recovery using fixed SAE dictionaries.
End-to-end SAEs reduced output loss, while normalization improved their activation explained variance.
Correcting underestimated feature activations left most Pythia-70m reconstruction error intact.
Corpus-trained SAEs explained only 48.8% of variance on the entity activations.
The best full-replacement method retained substantial divergence and poor benchmark accuracy.
TopK scaling fits retained irreducible loss despite improved reconstruction.
Correcting underestimated feature activations explained little of Gated SAEs' gains, and substantial error remained.
JumpReLU modestly improved fidelity over Gated SAEs and roughly matched TopK.
Fine-tuning with distribution-matching and mean-squared-error losses reduced the cross-entropy gap by 20–50%; substantial excess cross-entropy remained.
Magnitude bypass reduced high-norm reconstruction error, but the fraction of variance explained stayed negative.
Architecture changes produced modest reconstruction gains or increased error, depending on the model.
Matching-pursuit SAEs lowered reconstruction error but worsened sparse probing.
BatchTopK and L1 crosscoder errors retained similar amounts of chat behavior.
End-to-end training worsened activation reconstruction at matched output loss.
A rank-24 bottleneck barely reduced measured dark matter in Gemma-2-2B.
Uniformly shrinking activations barely changed GPT2-small's output distribution.
Replacement-aware training, LISTA, and KL fine-tuning increased single-layer reconstruction error.
Cosine scoring left overall reconstruction fidelity essentially unchanged when an additional loss trained inactive SAE features.

counting_note: Each group counts distinct sources for this claim. The same source can appear in more than one group or claim; counts are not votes.

untested.what: A quantitative causal attribution showing that most dark matter comes from training artifacts rather than representation structure.
untested.basis: This gap is inferred from the experimental scope, rather than explicitly identified by all the papers. arXiv:2404.16014#R4 isolates shrinkage correction from changes in learned directions; arXiv:2509.20784#r4 compares corpus-trained features on entity activations; lw:4tEnmAwFNtz9zJ6cz#r20 compares reconstruction and error compounding; arXiv:2605.31245#r12 compares architecture reconstruction MSE. These comparisons do not quantitatively partition total reconstruction error into training artifacts and representation structure. In arXiv:2404.16014#R2 and arXiv:2404.16014#R3, shrinkage correction does not measure its share of total error or exclude representation structure as a cause. Counts keys versions.V6.coverage_by_operation and versions.V6.studies_with_untested_parts summarize coverage but do not supply such a partition.

untested.what: Whether near-perfect reconstruction extends to corpus-scale arbitrary token activations while preserving downstream behaviour.
untested.basis: arXiv:2509.20784#r1, arXiv:2509.20784#r2 and arXiv:2509.20784#r3 report dataset-matched entity reconstruction; arXiv:2509.20784#r4 evaluates corpus-trained features on entity activations. Downstream replacement fidelity is unmeasured even in the tested static final-token entity setting. The checker additionally identifies Wikipedia and MATH500 training-source ablations in Appendix C.1/Table 2 and a large WikiData activation-pool sweep in Section 4.3. These experiments leave corpus-scale arbitrary-token generalization with preserved downstream behaviour unestablished; downstream loss is not measured. This gap is inferred from scope, rather than explicitly listed by the authors. versions.V6.coverage_by_operation.measurement does not establish this joint transfer.

untested.what: Size-identified tests of V6 at 10–100B and above 100B.
untested.basis: versions.V6.studies_by_size contains 1-10B, <1B and not stated, with no 10-100B or >100B entries. versions.V6.coverage_by_operation likewise provides no size-identified coverage in those larger bins. Unspecified model sizes cannot establish coverage there.

wording_issues.phrase: mostly reflects how SAEs are trained
wording_issues.issue: On GPT-2 small layer 8, fixed-mask, fixed-decoder refinement improves reconstruction and downstream cross-entropy but closes only part of the ReLU–TopK gap. On GELU-1L, rescaling and shifting resolve shrinkage but explain only a small part of the gated-SAE performance gain. Neither result quantifies the fraction of total error attributable to training. Pythia-70m decoder fine-tuning reduces MSE by a reported fraction of 0.088; Pythia-160M iSAE-ME also improves MSE over TopK. These establish training-sensitive improvements without a causal majority attribution.

The measures distinguish activation reconstruction, downstream KL/CE, latent error ratios and token-stratum FVE. GPT2-small end-to-end SAEs reconstruct activation directions worse than local SAEs at similar CE loss increase. On Gemma-2-2B base, replacement-aware LISTA plus KL fine-tuning worsens single-layer RRE while improving the fitted error-compounding bound; these measurements precede encoder tuning. Separately, full-replacement training improvements substantially reduce downstream divergence, supporting training dependence of that outcome. Gemma 2 2B base/chat crosscoder latent error ratios measure a specific shrinkage artifact. On Qwen3-8B layer 18 at 500M tokens, architectural changes strongly improve highest-norm-quartile reconstruction while aggregate FVE remains essentially unchanged with auxiliary dead-latent loss enabled. Improvement in one measure does not establish improvement in the others.

wording_issues.phrase: shrinks with better architectures or end-to-end training
wording_issues.issue: The direction depends on the measure and setting. GPT2-small end-to-end SAEs reconstruct activation directions worse than local SAEs at similar CE loss increase. On Gemma-2-2B base, replacement-aware LISTA plus KL fine-tuning worsens pre-encoder-tuning single-layer RRE while improving the fitted error-compounding bound; full-replacement training separately reduces downstream divergence. Pythia-160M layer 12 AbsTopK and iSAE increase MSE relative to TopK, challenging the shrinking-error component; DINOv2-Base AbsTopK gives a small MSE reduction. A parallel rank-24 bottleneck on Gemma-2-2B base layer 12 improves explained variance without substantially reducing the reported dark matter.

wording_issues.phrase: rather than reflecting structure in the model's representation
wording_issues.issue: The comparisons establish reconstruction sensitivity without causally excluding representation structure. Gated-SAE results on GELU-1L and Pythia-2.8B establish training-dependent improvements. The static entity-activation study reports no causal partition or residual-error structure analysis; its authors attribute high-fidelity reconstruction to intrinsic sparsifiability. The Pythia-160M/DINOv2 architecture study does not separate training-induced error from representation structure, and its remaining-gap discussion concerns code stability. Gemma-2-2B replacement-aware training improves the fitted error-compounding bound while worsening single-layer RRE; neither outcome partitions the causes of error. Absence of these analyses should not be described as an explicit acknowledgment by every study.

method_sensitivity.what: On GPT2-small residual activations, end-to-end SAEs reconstruct activation directions worse than local SAEs at similar CE loss increase. Norm suppression alone does not determine reconstruction-error direction. Evaluation-time layer-norm normalization improves explained variance, but the overall comparison remains similar; this does not demonstrate reduced activation dark matter. On Gemma-2-2B base, replacement-aware training improves downstream replacement fidelity. Separately, before encoder tuning, replacement-aware LISTA plus KL fine-tuning raises single-layer RRE from 0.339987 to 0.399214 while lowering the fitted error-compounding bound from 0.0556639 to 0.0282006. These outcomes establish metric-dependent training effects without attributing most dark matter to training.

method_sensitivity.factor: Training sparsity, encoder optimization and shrinkage correction
method_sensitivity.what: On GPT-2 small layer 8, fixed-mask, fixed-decoder refinement increases ReLU activations on average relative to raw encoder activations, consistent with correcting L1 shrinkage. TopK refinement has no upward bias and is smaller in magnitude. Refinement improves reconstruction but closes only part of the ReLU–TopK gap. In the 1-layer model's post-activation MLP site, gradient pursuit improves loss recovered with the dictionary fixed, while dictionary quality also depends on training L0. These comparisons distinguish encoder and dictionary limitations and establish partial training dependence; they do not establish majority attribution to training or exclude representation structure.

As method-comparison context, JumpReLU consistently improves fidelity over Gated and matches or often slightly improves upon TopK across tested Gemma 2 9B base sites. TopK already avoids an L1 sparsity penalty; these comparisons do not identify the predominant source of dark matter. Gated gains vary by Pythia/Gemma site and establish partial training dependence. On Pythia-160M layer 12, AbsTopK and iSAE increase reconstruction MSE relative to TopK, challenging the shrinking-error component in those conditions. On DINOv2-Base ImageNet-1k patch tokens, AbsTopK produces a small MSE reduction and iSAE also improves reconstruction. The Pythia increases and DINOv2 reductions are distinct outcomes.

On Gemma2-2B/9B and Llama3.1-8B, dataset-matched threshold SAEs achieve near-perfect reconstruction of static final-token entity activations. Corpus-trained GemmaScope/LlamaScope comparators achieve a reported aggregate R2 of 48.8% on those activations; this aggregates evaluated models and is not a per-model value. The comparison establishes training-regime sensitivity, without establishing that every scope comparator uses JumpReLU or demonstrating a V6 limitation. The pack also reports a capacity threshold for near-perfect reconstruction, without displaying the numerical grid.

method_sensitivity.factor: Token norm stratum and auxiliary dead-latent loss
method_sensitivity.what: On Qwen3-8B-Base layer 18 after 500M training tokens, cosine scoring dramatically improves highest-norm-quartile FVE while aggregate FVE remains essentially unchanged with auxiliary dead-latent loss. Magnitude bypass also sharply reduces Q4 error: FVE is −0.200 versus −183.5 for standard scoring, using within-quartile variance normalization. Negative final FVE does not negate this observed error reduction or establish aggregate improvement. The text-only verdict reports aggregate gains without auxiliary loss in 50M-token Qwen3-8B and Gemma-2-2B comparisons. Architecture effects depend on token stratum and training recipe.

On Gemma-2-2b layer 12, 32k-wide Matching Pursuit SAEs trained on 300M tokens reconstruct better than BatchTopK/Matryoshka comparators but have worse sparse probing at k=1 and k=16 and worse absorption scores; degenerate absorption is a proposed explanation. Standard Matching Pursuit uses L0 approximately 85 and 265; Static Matching Pursuit uses L0=85 and reconstructs slightly better than standard Matching Pursuit. Improvement magnitudes relative to traditional comparators are unquantified, so these results do not establish predominant training attribution. Worse feature-quality metrics do not themselves limit V6. For Gemma 2 2B base/chat crosscoders, BatchTopK removes a latent shrinkage artifact while leaving behaviour recoverable from the error largely unchanged.
